title: The report puts one apostrophe before a line starting with =, +, - or @
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure Require Tech Story is off (Settings, then the Work Orders tab).
  • Create a work order for this test, work order 1, with five labor lines, each with the description "leaking": line 1 titled "=Replace hose", line 2 titled "+Replace hose", line 3 titled "-Replace hose", line 4 titled "@Replace hose" and line 5 titled "Replace hose".
  • Have lines 1 to 5 completed with no tech story, and work order 1 completed and invoiced today as invoice A.
  • Use a plain text editor (Notepad on Windows, or TextEdit set to plain text on a Mac) to open the downloaded file, so you see its text exactly as it was written.
  • Use Google Sheets (File, then Import, then Upload) to open downloaded files, so accented letters and character counts read correctly.
  • Start on Reports, then Export Reports in the Reports left menu, with the Export Report dialog open.
custom_steps:
1. Pick Customer Invoice in the Report Name list.
  2. Set the date range to today.
  3. Click Download.
  4. Open the downloaded file in the plain text editor.
  5. Search the file for "Replace hose".
  6. Open the downloaded file in Google Sheets.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Customer Invoice is picked in Report Name.

Step 2:

  • The date range shows today's date.

Step 3:

  • A Customer Invoice file downloads.

Step 4:

  • The file opens as plain text.

Step 5:

  • Five lines of work order 1's invoice A are found (a line's text may sit inside double quotes, which belong to the file format).
  • Line 1's text starts with one apostrophe and then "=Replace hose - leaking".
  • Line 2's text starts with one apostrophe and then "+Replace hose - leaking".
  • Line 3's text starts with one apostrophe and then "-Replace hose - leaking".
  • Line 4's text starts with one apostrophe and then "@Replace hose - leaking".
  • Line 5's text starts with "Replace hose - leaking", with no apostrophe in front.
  • None of the five has two apostrophes in front.

Step 6:

  • In Google Sheets, each of lines 1 to 4's ItemDescription cells holds text that includes "Replace hose - leaking".
  • None of the four cells shows a calculated value or an error such as #ERROR! or #NAME?.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "What Are You Doing / Why Are You Doing It?" (Title and Description), Confluence 845348896, version 16 (27 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11257, story SV-10132 (Story 3, What Reaches QuickBooks)

  • S3-R8a: “In the downloadable Customer Invoice report only, a line text that starts with =, +, -, @, a tab or a carriage return gets one apostrophe in front of it, so a spreadsheet opens it as text and never as a formula. This is the same guard the newer report downloads already use. The old line always started with "What are you doing?: ", so it could not open as a formula; a line that now starts with the Title can. The live QuickBooks sync never carries the apostrophe.”
  • S3-R4: “The same text is used by the live QuickBooks sync and by the downloadable Customer Invoice report. Built at the same moment, the two never show different text for the same line, apart from the leading apostrophe the report adds in S3-R8a. An invoice already in QuickBooks keeps its old text there (S3-N1, S3-E4).”
  • S3-R8: “The values themselves are unchanged. Nothing is trimmed, truncated, re-cased or escaped that is not trimmed, truncated, re-cased or escaped today, other than the shortening described in S3-R7 and the removal of spaces and line breaks at the very end of the whole line (S3-R3), and the apostrophe in S3-R8a.”

From: Product's answers to our questions 9-14 (Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, Google Doc 1QcT7FRZci6AhYcI33HUac-Oob03-gCnCOKn2NFHMLjA, saved in po-answers-2026-10-27/), read 28 Oct 2026

  • Answer 11: “11. Testers should expect plain text. In the downloaded Customer Invoice report, a line starting with =, +, -, @, a tab or a carriage return gets one apostrophe in front, the same guard our newer report downloads use. QuickBooks never gets the apostrophe. The build has no guard yet, so please log a bug against new S3-R8a.”

Not yet checked against a build by us: the QA build (sv10130.qa.shopview.com, QuickBooks host qb1.qa.shopview.com) and staging carry this change, and this case has not been run on either.
